💵 ADVANCED: Dollar Liquidity — The Hidden Market Driver

Dollar liquidity is the fuel that powers global markets. When USD availability tightens, assets struggle. When it flows freely, risk assets rally.

Understanding the mechanics:

- The Fed controls base liquidity through reserve policy
- Banks create secondary liquidity through credit expansion
- Offshore eurodollar markets amplify or restrict flow
- Treasury operations drain or inject cash daily

Real market impact right now:

The US 10-year Treasury yield sits at 4.15 percent because liquidity conditions are moderating. When the Fed reverse repo facility dropped from 2.5 trillion to under 500 billion earlier this year, it injected massive liquidity into the system. Bonds rallied hard as cash found new homes.

Watch these liquidity indicators:

- Fed balance sheet size (expanding = more liquidity)
- Reverse repo usage (declining = liquidity entering markets)
- Treasury General Account (TGA) balance at the Fed
- Credit spreads on investment grade bonds

PRO TIP: When the TGA drops significantly, Treasury spends money into the economy. This boosts liquidity and typically supports bond prices. Track the daily Treasury statement for edge.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

📊 TECHNICAL: Ichimoku Cloud Basics — All-in-One Chart System

The Ichimoku Cloud gives you trend, momentum, and support/resistance in one glance. It looks complex but breaks down simply.

Five key components:

- Tenkan-sen (Conversion Line): 9-period midpoint, shows short-term momentum
- Kijun-sen (Base Line): 26-period midpoint, confirms trend direction
- Senkou Span A: Average of Tenkan and Kijun, projected forward
- Senkou Span B: 52-period midpoint, projected forward
- Chikou Span: Closing price, shifted back 26 periods

The Cloud (Kumo) is formed by Senkou A and B. Price above cloud = bullish. Price below cloud = bearish. Price in cloud = neutral or transition zone.

Practical example with TLT (20-plus Year Treasury ETF):

TLT recently broke above its daily cloud at 93.50 after months below. The Tenkan crossed above Kijun at 94.20, confirming bullish momentum. Traders who entered on cloud breakout captured the move to 97.80.

How to trade it:

- Enter long when price breaks above cloud with Tenkan above Kijun
- Enter short when price breaks below cloud with Tenkan below Kijun
- Cloud thickness shows strength (thick = strong support/resistance)
- Chikou Span above price confirms bullish bias

SMART MONEY RULE: The best Ichimoku setups occur when all elements align. Wait for cloud breakout, line cross, and Chikou confirmation before entering.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

🎯 THREE DAILY TRADING TIPS

1. WATCH THE BOND AUCTION CALENDAR

This week brings 2-year and 5-year Treasury auctions. Weak demand (high yield, low bid-to-cover) often triggers selloffs in bond futures. Strong auctions can spark intraday rallies. Check auction results at 1 PM EST and trade the immediate reaction.

2. FADE OVERNIGHT GAPS IN QUIET MARKETS

When ZN (10-Year Note futures) gaps at the open without major news, the gap often fills by mid-morning. If ZN opens up 6 ticks on low volume, short near the open with tight stops. Target gap fill for quick scalps.

3. CORRELATION TRADE: BONDS VS MORTGAGE REITS

Mortgage REITs like AGNC and NLY move opposite to yields. When the 10-year yield drops, these REITs rally. Use this correlation for confirmation. If bonds rally but mortgage REITs lag, the bond move might be weak or false.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

⚠️ RISK MANAGEMENT: Money Management Rules That Save Accounts

Position sizing matters more than entry timing. You can have a 60 percent win rate and still blow your account with poor money management.

The core principle:

Never risk more than 1-2 percent of your total capital on a single trade. If you have a 10,000 dollar account, risk only 100-200 dollars per position.

Calculate position size properly:

- Determine your stop loss distance in dollars or ticks
- Divide your risk amount by stop distance
- This gives you maximum position size
- Adjust contract quantity or share count accordingly

Real scenario with ZB (30-Year Bond futures):

Your account: 25,000 dollars. Risk per trade: 1 percent = 250 dollars. Stop loss: 8 ticks (256 dollars per contract). Position size: 250 divided by 256 = 0.97 contracts. Trade only 1 contract.

Advanced money management tactics:

- Scale into winners, never into losers
- Reduce size after consecutive losses (drawdown protection)
- Increase size slowly after winning streaks
- Never go all-in, even on high-conviction setups

Daily loss limits protect capital:

Set a maximum daily loss (3 percent of capital). If you hit it, stop trading immediately. Emotional revenge trading destroys more accounts than bad strategies.

PRO TIP: Keep a position sizing calculator on your phone. Before every trade, calculate exact size based on stop distance and account risk. Never estimate or trade by feel.
